requirements.requirement: Limit account datauser to 100MB of storage under /srv/data on node1, enforced by the filesystem itself
requirements.summary: Executor created datauser, built an ext4-backed loopback filesystem mounted at /srv/data with native ext4 quota support (tune2fs -O quota), and set a 100MB (102400 KB) block quota via setquota. Enforcement was directly demonstrated twice: pre-reboot, a 90MB write succeeded but a subsequent 50MB write failed with 'Disk quota exceeded' with repquota showing usage pinned at the 102400 KB hard limit; post-reboot, a 110MB write also failed at the same boundary. This is filesystem-level (kernel ext4 quota) enforcement, not an application-level check, satisfying the contract.

overall_summary: The core task — a filesystem-enforced 100MB quota for datauser under /srv/data on node1 — is satisfied with direct before/during/after evidence of enforcement, including survival across an observed reboot (boot ID changed 67f3a44b→3be1e874, quota intact and still enforced afterward). The one notable gap is a leftover failed quotaon.service unit visible in the final node state that the executor did not clean up, which is a minor but real piece of operational residue.
limitations: The failed quotaon.service unit's downstream effects (e.g., whether it will re-trigger warnings or affect future boots) were not further investigated by the executor or captured in evidence.
No evidence was captured of behavior for other users (e.g., root or another account) confirming they are unaffected by the quota, though this was not required by the task.

operational_hygiene.summary: Most executor commands were necessary and purposeful: user creation, loopback filesystem build, fstab registration, quota configuration, and bounded enforcement tests with cleanup of test files (cmd-cf4af926faff40d0, cmd-78bdc00c310d4506, cmd-ac66d50da136439b) — no abandoned test data remained. However, the after_executor snapshot shows a new failed systemd unit, quotaon.service ('Enable File System Quotas'), that was not present at before_prepare and was never remediated (e.g., via systemctl reset-failed or masking if unneeded). This traces back to the initial quotaon invocation on external quota files (cmd-886c1ad19e064ede), which the executor correctly worked around by switching to the native ext4 quota feature (cmd-eacc5e338efd431b), but the now-orphaned/failing quotaon.service unit was left in a failed state through the final reboot, constituting residue on the managed node even though it did not block functional quota enforcement.
